paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God gives the land, and He also gives the borders. He tells Israel, "for I have given you the land to possess" (Numbers 33:53), then draws the lines on all four sides and says, "This will be your land, defined by its borders on all sides" (Numbers 34:12). Nothing here is left foggy. The land is a gift, and the One who gives it also says where it begins and ends.

So why the hard words about driving out the people and destroying the idols? God warns that anyone left behind will become "barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides" (Numbers 33:55). I can't tell you more than the text says about how that plays out, but God clearly cares what Israel lets settle in beside them. Friend, I know what one little thing hanging around the bakery does, and it never stays little.

And look who gets the clipboard: God names Eleazar and Joshua, then one leader from each tribe, and Caleb son of Jephunneh is first on the list (Numbers 34:17-19). The inheritance is handed out by lot, through people He picked by name (Numbers 33:54). So here's your takeaway, baker: whatever God gives you, take it, and keep out what He says to keep out. The story isn't over, either, and there's more still to come.
